title: JRE 2358 - Chadd Wright
guestBio: Chadd Wright is a retired Navy SEAL, endurance athlete, speaker, and entrepreneur. He is a cofounder of the Three of Seven Project, a health and self-improvement program for the body, soul, and spirit.

recap:
Joe sits down with Chadd Wright, a retired Navy SEAL turned entrepreneur and endurance athlete, to dig into what it takes to build an elite mindset and push the human body to its limits. Wright brings the kind of no-nonsense perspective you'd expect from someone who's gone through the crucible of SEAL training and come out the other side still wanting to challenge himself further.

The conversation centers around Wright's Three of Seven Project, which is his answer to a pretty simple question: how do you get better at everything? The program takes a holistic approach, addressing the body, the soul, and the spirit. It's not just about getting jacked or running ultramarathons, though Wright does both. It's about building a framework for continuous self-improvement that actually sticks.

Wright breaks down what separates people who talk about getting better from people who actually do it. He's spent enough time in extreme environments to know that mental fortitude isn't something you're born with, it's something you build through deliberate practice and exposure to discomfort. Joe and Chadd explore how Navy SEAL training functions as a crucible for this kind of development, and why that same methodology can apply to regular people who want to optimize their lives.

The discussion gets into the weeds on discipline, the importance of having a clear why, and how most people fail because they haven't actually figured out what they're working toward. Wright emphasizes that it's not about being superhuman, it's about being systematic. Show up, do the work, compound the gains over time.

There's also ground covered on the intersection of physical training and psychological resilience. Wright argues that pushing your body teaches you things about yourself that sitting on the couch never will. When you're truly uncomfortable, you learn what you're actually made of. That knowledge then transfers to every other area of life.

Byway, Joe brings up Nobody 2, the Universal Pictures action film hitting theaters August 15, which ties into the conversation about peak performance and the kind of physical capability that makes for entertaining cinema.
